title: Review: pkix-revocation-http since 24701180 (async fetcher + cache)
close_reason:
All 27 children are closed. Ten were superseded by PKIX-cr8 (the re-filed hardening epic) and resolved there; the remaining seven -- .12 .13 .14 .17 .18 .19 .20 -- were closed directly in commits ef1fd31a and a829edc8.

Three of those seven turned out to be more than their P2/P3/P4 labels suggested: .19 was filed as a naming opinion but the comparator's parameter names were inverted at its only call site (correct behaviour, lying signature); .13's three listed options were all breaking or no-ops, while a fourth existed that was neither; .18's own counter-argument misstated how Cargo features work, so the proposed fix would have forced x509-ocsp/sha1/sha2 on CRL-only consumers. Two (.12, .17) were closed the way the bead itself recommended, as recorded reasoning rather than code. One (.20) was already most of the way fixed by the cr8 work.

The epic's own note said 'maintainer risk: MEDIUM -- two correctness bugs (cache time-source mismatch, rollback TOCTOU) are real'. Both of those were among the ten handled under PKIX-cr8.
